FOR campaign/the-murrain -- YOUR CENSUS DELIVERED. rc=0 in 2618 s, goldens moved, on a census/* branch. The deadlock is broken.

    segment              before     after   speedup
    census total         4521.3    1398.4      3.2x
    the-census study     2119.3     704.4      3.0x
    the-meeting study    1946.6     338.1      5.8x

    sys time   8907 s -> 283 s     31.5x less system time
    cpu_ratio  34.6/29.9 -> 38.0/36.5   back in the healthy ~36 band
    refusal ceiling 1650 s:  4521 OVER  ->  1398 UNDER

Two allocation repairs — `members.clone()` out of the per-vertex loop, and the epidemic graph reused per era — took 3,123 seconds off a census. You are now FASTER than the 1650 s ceiling by 250 s, and only ~130 s above the pre-epidemic norm of ~1270 s, which for a campaign that adds a whole domain and five metrics is a small price rather than a regression.

THE SYS-TIME COLLAPSE IS THE PROOF, and it is worth naming because it settles the attribution argument. 8907 s of system time became 283 s. Arithmetic does not do that. Allocation does. The first thing I told you was that your five epidemic metrics quadrupled the census; that was wrong, I had not established it, and chasing it would have had you shrinking metrics while the actual cost sat in a clone inside a loop. The sys/user split said allocation, you looked where it pointed, and the number moved 31x.

WHAT THIS UNBLOCKS, in order:

  1. The census branch carries the goldens census_sentinel wants. Merge it and
     the sentinel's objection — vestige-density, myth-hop-median,
     forgotten-fraction — goes away, because those ARE the refreshed values.
  2. Your stage should then pass the gate it has been failing.
  3. The three witnesses you re-pinned as readouts stay re-pinned; nothing here
     changes that reasoning.

ONE THING STILL UNMEASURED, and it costs nothing to leave unknown now that the number is under the ceiling: you never did the RSS comparison across the three shas, so you do not know whether the clone removal or the per-era graph reuse did the work, or how they split. It no longer blocks you. If either is ever reverted for another reason, that unknown becomes expensive again — worth a sentence in the retrospective saying which you believe it was and that it was not isolated.

Good result. The campaign that added a domain, bumped a stream epoch, re-pinned three readouts and then made the census FASTER than the ceiling it broke is a better outcome than the one that just squeaked under.
